title: Dynam3D: Dynamic Layered 3D Tokens Empower VLM for Vision-and-Language Navigation

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The prose claims Dynam3D 'achieves modest improvements of approximately 1-2% in navigation success rate (SR)' on R2R-CE relative to g3D-LF/Uni-NaVid and 'outperforming NaVid by approximately 3-5% in Success Rate (SR) on REVERIE-CE and NavRAG-CE'. Table 1 shows Dynam3D R2R-CE Val SR = 52.9 vs g3D-LF 47.2 (+5.7 points) and vs Uni-NaVid 47.0 (+5.9 points); Table 2 shows REVERIE-CE Val SR = 40.1 vs NaVid 26.6 (+13.5 points) and NavRAG-CE 24.7 vs NaVid 19.4 (+5.3 points). The reported percentages (1-2%, 3-5%) do not match the table deltas by a factor of ~3-4x on R2R-CE and ~3-4x on REVERIE-CE (13.5 points vs '3-5%'). Even under the most generous reading no metric in the tables produces a 1-2% R2R-CE gain. This is a numeric text-vs-table contradiction material to the paper's headline performance claim.

The text states: 'we perform ablation by degrading the quality of 3D instance and zone embeddings through feature dropout and spatial jitter to evaluate sensitivity. Table 7 shows that while navigation success rate (SR) decreases with noise addition, it degrades significantly more when 3D representation quality is compromised.' However, Table 7 contains only four rows (no noise / SLAM-only / depth-only / both), i.e., exclusively SLAM and depth noise conditions. No feature-dropout or spatial-jitter representation-quality ablation rows are present in the referenced table, so the claim that 'Table 7 shows ... it degrades significantly more when 3D representation quality is compromised' is not supported by the table it cites. The robustness section also asserts 'the 3D-aware representations obtained by our model ... remain sufficient' despite the absence of the described representation-degradation experiment.

summary: Exhaustive lenient-mode verification of 'Dynam3D: Dynamic Layered 3D Tokens Empower VLM for Vision-and-Language Navigation' (cs.CV; 34 snippets: 16 sections, 7 equations, 7 tables, 4 figures) found 2 above-threshold findings, both medium-confidence text-table data inconsistencies. (1) Section 4.1 understates the table-reported SR gains: the prose claims ~1-2% improvement on R2R-CE and ~3-5% on REVERIE-CE/NavRAG-CE, whereas Tables 1-2 show +5.7/+5.9 percentage points on R2R-CE and +13.5 points on REVERIE-CE (vs NaVid), a ~3-4x discrepancy. (2) Section 4.6 attributes to Table 7 a feature-dropout/spatial-jitter representation-quality ablation ('degrades significantly more when 3D representation quality is compromised') that Table 7 does not contain; the table covers only SLAM and depth noise. The mathematical content (Eqs. 1-7) was checked and found internally consistent (projection, frustum culling, instance encoder, contrastive/subspace distillation losses), the computational-cost arithmetic in Section 4.5 sums correctly (455 ms = 83+315+57; 649 ms = 83+540+26), the ablation ordering (Patch > Instance > Zone) is supported by Table 6, and the abstract/conclusion/results are mutually consistent with no conclusion-invalidating contradictions. Both flagged findings are conservative-direction reporting inconsistencies rather than result-inflating fraud, so the paper is judged NEEDS_REVIEW pending correction of the stated percentages and the Table 7 claim.
